statement.text:
T2: Thread around a cylinder
One end of a thread is tied into a loop of length \(L>2\pi R\). A cylinder of radius \(R\) passes through the loop. The coefficient of friction between thread and cylinder is \(\mu\). The free end is pulled parallel to the cylinder axis, as indicated by the arrow in the photograph, while the cylinder is held at rest.

If \(L>L_0\), the loop can slide along the cylinder without changing shape. Otherwise friction locks it in place, and increasing the pulling force eventually breaks the thread. Find \(L_0\). Neglect the thread weight. The thread does not twist when pulled.
The following integral may be useful:
\[2\int\sqrt{1+x^2}\,dx=x\sqrt{1+x^2}+\operatorname{arcsinh}x,\qquad \operatorname{arcsinh}x=\ln\left(x+\sqrt{1+x^2}\right).\]

solution.text:
T2: Thread around a cylinder
Let \(P\) be the pulled point and \(O\) the top point of the loop. The loop is a non-planar curve with a cusp at \(P\). Cut the cylinder along the generator through \(P\) and unfold its side. Set the origin at \(O\), \(x\) around the circumference and \(z\) parallel to the axis in the pulling direction.


At impending axial slip, friction is parallel to \(z\), and the \(x\)-component of tension \(T_x\) is constant by force balance. A small segment has circumferential width \(dx\), angular span \(d\varphi=dx/R\), and normal reaction
\[dN=2T_x\sin(d\varphi/2)\simeq T_x\frac{dx}{R},\qquad df=\mu\,dN.\]
The \(z\)-components of the end tensions differ by \(T_xz''dx\). Balancing them against friction gives
\[T_xz''dx=df,\qquad z''=\frac\mu R,\qquad z(0)=z'(0)=0,\qquad z(x)=\frac{\mu x^2}{2R}.\]
The required loop length is the arc length across one full circumference on the unfolded surface:
\[L_0=2\int_0^{\pi R}\sqrt{1+\left(\frac{\mu x}{R}\right)^2}\,dx=\frac{2R}{\mu}\int_0^{\pi\mu}\sqrt{1+\xi^2}\,d\xi.\]
\[L_0=\pi R\sqrt{1+(\pi\mu)^2}+\frac R\mu\operatorname{arcsinh}(\pi\mu).\]
A shorter loop cannot satisfy this force-balanced sliding geometry. As \(\mu\to0\), \(\operatorname{arcsinh}(\pi\mu)\sim\pi\mu\), so \(L_0\to2\pi R\), the circumference. The answer field uses the equivalent logarithmic form. Original marking tables remain in the PDF.
